name: ktkit
description: A spec-driven development toolkit for Claude Code: seventeen skills covering the path from a problem somebody described in chat to a reviewed spec, an executed change, and a durable record of both. raise-issue frames that problem first -- it labels every fact with where it came from and how far it can be trusted, refuses to name a cause, and blocks until you confirm it understood the right problem. chain runs that path as one closed loop -- it resolves the open questions each phase raises by dispatching resolver subagents, records every answer in an append-only ledger the later phases read instead of re-deriving, and stops only for what could not be settled and would be expensive to get wrong. docs-review audits a document set with a team of agents that run concurrently and challenge each other's findings. spec-recon adds the axis a document reviewer cannot reach — it measures source code, binary artifacts and version-control state, and gates every claim that something is missing behind an agent that tries to refute it. analyze-feat, rca, cr-delta, feat-req-specs and bug-fix-specs turn a request into a reviewed specification -- cr-delta answers the question a change request asks and a feature request does not, which finished work this undoes, and answers it from the run's task ledger rather than by re-reading the repository; feat-req-execute and bug-fix-execute carry it out; ccompact and ccontinue keep a long pipeline alive across compaction; escalation-ladder resolves unknowns from the repository before asking you; confirm-with-me gates a single irreversible step; translate-file translates a file without touching its identifiers; help prints an index of all of them, and a page per skill that is checked against that skill's own argument surface rather than written once and left to rot. Every skill writes to one fixed artifact root, runs a preflight that proves a capability with a real request instead of trusting a tool's own error message, and refuses to start when spec-kit or superpowers is missing rather than quietly doing something else.
